Create a Rust-compatible R-CMD-check Workflow

Source: R/42C_use_workflow_rust_compatible_check.R
use_workflow_rust_compatible_check.Rd

Copies the built-in R-CMD-Check.yaml workflow template to the target package's .github/workflows/ directory, so that R CMD check runs on GitHub Actions with a toolchain that can download, compile and link Rust crates (packages built on extendr/rextendr).

Usage

use_workflow_rust_compatible_check(path = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Character. Path to the package root directory. If NULL (the default), uses the current working directory.

overwrite

Logical. If TRUE, overwrite an existing workflow file. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

Invisibly returns the path to the created workflow file.

Why not the usethis workflow

usethis::use_github_action("check-standard") only sets up R and then calls R CMD check on a matrix of operating systems. For packages with Rust code this is not enough:

  • No Rust toolchain is installed, so the runner default is used. On Windows that default is an MSVC toolchain, while R and Rtools are GNU based, so the static library produced by cargo cannot be linked, and the resulting build noise (cargo warnings, linker messages) makes R CMD check report a WARNING.

The template used here follows the official extendr CI:

  • dtolnay/rust-toolchain installs the requested toolchain, and on Windows additionally the x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target that Rtools can link.

  • The R matrix covers Windows, macOS, Ubuntu release and Ubuntu devel, with fail-fast: false so one broken platform does not hide the others.

  • R_REMOTES_NO_ERRORS_FROM_WARNINGS keeps remotes/pak download noise from turning into check failures.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
temp <- tempdir()
usethis::create_package(temp)
use_workflow_rust_compatible_check(temp)
use_workflow_rust_compatible_check(temp, overwrite = TRUE)
} # }
